reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's protective care for the Hebrew people throughout. Multiple passages show explicit distinction made between Israel and Egypt: God protects Israel's livestock from disease while Egyptian livestock dies (9:6-7), shields Goshen from the plague of flies (8:22-23), and ensures no animal of Israel is struck (9:6). Most significantly, God provides the Passover instructions specifically to protect Israeli households from the death of the firstborn (12:12-13), marking them with blood to ensure 'no destructive plague will touch you.' The text emphasizes that 'among all the Israelites not a dog will bark' while Egypt is devastated, and God ultimately 'passed over the houses of the sons of Israel' (12:27). The entire narrative of liberation from slavery demonstrates God's active intervention to preserve and deliver the Hebrew people from harm and bondage.
